findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:230-255 [HIGH] The claimed exact causal envelope is validated only by event type + verdictId. A concurrent mutation can keep those two fields while changing hostId/sessionId/keyId/decision/materialDigest/storyFilesHash/validationDigest/promptDigest; assertExactQuorumAppend then accepts and the immutable transaction commits the forged L4 host_verdict row. This contradicts CHK-002 happy:1/adversarial:1 and the new process-fact atomic-persistence claim. Compare every persisted row against the full canonical event derived from the returned verdict/bindings (or bind exact generated bytes/digests), and add a focused mutation test that preserves verdictId while altering a gate-consumed field and proves refusal/rollback. The same exact-byte ownership rule should govern ignored verdict-file rollback: lines 321-326 delete a concurrently changed file solely because verdictId still matches, so foreign bytes can be lost.
findings.resolvedReason: rootCause: exact append validation compared only type and verdictId, while verdict-file rollback also trusted verdictId instead of frozen bytes. repro: mutate decision on the sixth process event and mutate the sixth ignored JSON while retaining verdictId. reproTest: quorum-submit-smoke checks same-verdictId gate-field mutation refusal and concurrent JSON preservation. evidence: build PASS; quorum-submit-smoke PASS 27/27; commit 8d7b031bfa freezes full canonical event rows and JSON bytes, refuses mismatches, and preserves changed foreign bytes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:106-134,357-399 — HIGH coverage gap: the 27-intent evidence marks CHK-001 happy:0/happy:1/edge:0/adversarial:0/adversarial:2 and CHK-003 happy:0/adversarial:0 as covered by this smoke, but the smoke creates a synthetic temp repository with synthetic PASS evidence and invokes registry.get("quorum_submit") directly; it never invokes the worktree-local CLI, never runs the validation persistence path, never demonstrates the historical validation refusal/no-false-PASS boundary, and never proves the harness rejects a direct-handler-only shortcut. The only post-quorum check at lines 390-399 calls captureLifecycleMetadataTransaction and expects success after GREEN. The sole pre-dirty case at lines 579-592 is an untracked user file, not the separately required pre-dirty process-events plus staged/source/lifecycle cases. Thus several MUST intents are contradicted or only narratively attested while checklist evidence claims executable coverage. Add a bounded production-entry integration that runs node bin/lattice.js quorum_submit in a real fixture/worktree and exercises the validation persistence refusal on the RED implementation (or bind a concrete immutable historical receipt), plus the explicitly required pre-dirty categories; keep the existing fast handler matrix for fault injection.
findings.resolvedReason: rootCause: the prior smoke used a direct registry handler in a synthetic repo and never crossed the worktree-local CLI or validation canonical persistence boundary; the CLI also appended a post-handler codex_cli row that re-dirtied process-events. repro: node bin/lattice.js quorum_submit in the bounded fixture left a codex_cli delta, and validate on the historical six-row dirty baseline executed once then returned infra_failure. reproTest: quorum-submit-smoke production-entry cases cover clean CLI quorum, process-events/staged-source/lifecycle pre-dirt, and historical RED validation no-false-PASS. evidence: smoke PASS 27/27; validation payload status=fail allPass=false failureKind=infra_failure disposition=executed commandExecutions=1; original FAIL evidence and bytes preserved; commit 8d7b031bfa.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:398-410 and packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:489-512 — HIGH: same-material duplicate refusal trusts listVerdicts(), whose .lattice/autopilot-verdicts JSON files are gitignored/non-durable, instead of the canonical committed host_verdict events. Deleting that ignored directory after a successful quorum makes the same-material retry emit and commit another six rows, violating the explicit idempotency contract. The current smoke only tests while ignored JSON remains. Derive duplicate detection from committed process-events (exact runId/material binding), and add a regression that removes/loses the cache before retry.
findings.resolvedReason: rootCause: same-material duplicate refusal read gitignored autopilot-verdict JSON files, so cache loss erased duplicate authority despite committed host_verdict facts. repro: remove .lattice/autopilot-verdicts/B-quorum-smoke after a successful quorum and retry the same material. reproTest: quorum-submit-smoke same-material duplicate refusal survives deletion of the ignored verdict cache. evidence: smoke PASS 27/27; committedHostVerdictEvents reads HEAD process-events and retry leaves HEAD/event count unchanged in commit 8d7b031bfa.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:284-314 and packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:595-612 — HIGH: rollback claims to preserve malformed/foreign concurrent bytes verbatim but decodes the entire suffix as UTF-8, drops blank lines, and rejoins with a synthesized trailing newline. A concurrent non-UTF8 byte, blank line, or unterminated append is therefore rewritten/corrupted during rollback. The smoke covers only normalized JSON plus newline and asserts marker presence, not byte equality. Remove owned rows by exact byte spans while copying every other byte unchanged, and assert Buffer equality for malformed/non-UTF8 and unterminated foreign suffixes.
findings.resolvedReason: rootCause: rollback decoded the concurrent suffix as UTF-8, discarded blank lines, and synthesized a trailing newline, corrupting arbitrary foreign bytes. repro: append Buffer bytes containing blank lines, 0xff, NUL, JSON braces, and no terminal newline between verification and commit. reproTest: quorum-submit-smoke asserts exact Buffer equality after rollback. evidence: smoke PASS 27/27; rollback now removes only frozen owned Buffer spans and copies all remaining bytes unchanged in commit 8d7b031bfa.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:500-530,588-595 [HIGH] The repaired exact-byte ownership is registered only after captureOwnedVerdictOutput returns. submitLocalVerdict has already written both the host_verdict event and ignored verdict JSON; if the capture itself fails (a concurrent mutation changes the just-appended row, the verdict JSON is deleted/replaced before read, or the row is malformed), ownedEventRows/ownedVerdictFiles never receive that verdict. The catch therefore cannot remove even an unchanged generated JSON and may report all emitted verdicts rolled back while leaving the last command-owned outputs behind. This violates the all-row rollback and failed-attempt isolation contract. Record a provisional output identity before any fallible capture/validation, then either promote exact frozen bytes or conservatively preserve/report only genuinely changed bytes while removing unchanged command-owned outputs. Add a focused capture-time failure regression that verifies no unchanged verdict JSON/event residue and no false all-rolled-back diagnostic. Also ensure Buffer span removal is boundary/position anchored rather than suffix.indexOf(row) matching an owned row byte sequence embedded inside arbitrary foreign binary bytes (lines 297-317).
findings.resolvedReason: rootCause: quorum learned event/JSON ownership only through fallible post-write capture, so capture failure could leave unchanged generated outputs; suffix indexOf could also match embedded foreign bytes. fix: submitLocalVerdictWithOutputIdentity now returns process-event offset/exact bytes and verdict JSON path/bytes directly from the writer; quorum records them before validation, rollback uses absolute offsets and exact JSON compare. reproTests: capture-time failure removes unchanged row/JSON, changed JSON is preserved, embedded identical bytes survive. verification: build PASS and focused quorum-submit-smoke PASS 31/31 at 55f6d658. F-008 separately tracks non-cooperating direct append writers outside this specific capture-time ownership fix.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:493-535,588-595 and packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:775-859 — HIGH: owned rows/files are registered only after each submitLocalVerdict returns and captureOwnedVerdictOutput succeeds. If a foreign append occurs after row 1 is captured (afterVerdictWrite emittedCount=1), row 2 is then written after that foreign suffix; its capture sees foreign+row2 and throws, but rollback receives only row1/file1, leaving the generated row2 and ignored verdict JSON behind. This violates the all-emitted-rows rollback guarantee and makes the next retry refuse on dirty metadata. Existing foreign-suffix tests inject only after all six rows are registered. Add a between-row concurrency regression and ensure every write is rollback-owned even when post-write capture rejects (or verify the exact boundary before each next write and safely identify the just-written output on failure).
findings.resolvedReason: rootCause: the next verdict was written before checking whether bytes diverged after the prior captured row. fix: assertExactQuorumAppend now runs before every next submit; owned records use absolute offsets. reproTest: focused quorum-submit-smoke between-row foreign append preserves foreign bytes, writes no second row, removes all verdict JSON, and embedded identical-row binary remains byte-exact. verification: npm build PASS and focused quorum smoke PASS 30/30 at 67b0e2da64.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:509-556 [HIGH] F005/F006 are narrowed but the write-before gate is still a TOCTOU check, not an atomic boundary. A foreign append can land after assertExactQuorumAppend/eventStart (lines 509-514) and before submitLocalVerdict appends its row (515-528). The post-write prefix check compares only bytes before eventStart, so it accepts that prefix, then treats the foreign row at eventStart as the owned record (551-556). Validation fails, rollback deletes the foreign bytes at that absolute offset and leaves the actual generated host_verdict row behind—the exact foreign-data-loss + dirty-residue outcome this story forbids. The new between-row regression appends after afterVerdictWrite, so the next pre-write gate catches it before another verdict is written and does not cover this window. Make append ownership atomic/returned by the writer or capture a pre-write byte snapshot and identify/remove the actual generated append without claiming intervening foreign bytes; add a deterministic regression by wrapping appendProcessEvent to insert a foreign row immediately before the host_verdict append. RED/GREEN commits 7356ae0c/67b0e2da and focused 30/30 do not currently exercise this race.
findings.resolvedReason: rootCause: quorum previously inferred append ownership across a separate pre-write check, leaving a TOCTOU window where a foreign row could occupy the guessed offset. fix: 55f6d658 made appendProcessEvent return writer-owned start/end/eventBytes under the process-event lock; e95d88cf then moved every remaining production process-events writer onto the same locked raw/record primitives, eliminating the non-cooperative gap. REDs: 1f5cbb39 and 7ec6e7d7. verification: static incremental review confirms exact writer identity, timestamp preservation and atomic cross-host batch bytes; current focused quorum-submit-smoke PASS 32/32 including shared-lock production writer guard and writer-boundary rollback.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/process-events.ts:20-37, packages/main/src/handlers/cross-host-review.ts:646-655, and packages/main/src/core/dirty-gate-policy.ts:254-258 — HIGH: the writer-returned offset is atomic only relative to callers using appendProcessEvent/withMkdirLock. Two production writers still append process-events.jsonl directly: cross-host-review host-verdict batches and defaultAuditWriter dirty-gate audit rows. Either can append after the locked writer captures stat(start) but before its appendFileSync; the returned identity then points at the foreign row, quorum rollback can delete those foreign bytes and leave its generated host_verdict/JSON residue, recreating F-007. The GREEN test wraps StoryStore and inserts via originalAppend, so both writes cooperate with the lock and cannot exercise this window. Migrate all production process-event writers—at minimum these two—to the same locked raw append primitive (including batch identity where needed), and add a deterministic non-quorum-writer concurrency regression proving offsets/bytes stay exact and foreign rows survive rollback.
findings.resolvedReason: rootCause: cross_host_review and defaultAuditWriter directly appended process-events, bypassing the cooperative identity lock. fix: e95d88cf routes dirty-gate records through appendProcessEventRecord and the cross-host two-row batch through appendRawProcessEventBytes; both share .process-events-append.lock. Existing timestamps are preserved, missing timestamps are added once, and the two-host batch remains one combined newline-terminated append. RED 7ec6e7d7; focused quorum-submit-smoke PASS 32/32 and production-source guard reports zero direct appendFileSync process-event writers.
